utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Are there any preliminary matters to be raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just briefly and in private session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In private session briefly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- how much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: A minute or so between one and two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A one or so. Then could the witness already be escorted up to the door-step and then to enter the courtroom after that. We briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Javoric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Lukic will now continue his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would just kindly ask the usher to provide the witness with his statement from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Javoric --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if we could have D895 on our screens, please. That's the statement of this witness. We will need page 4 where we can find paragraph 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before you focus on paragraph 10, I'd like to ask you the following: Was it possible -- when call-up papers were being distributed or during mobilisation, was it possible to single out Muslims and Croats and not call them up?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would not have been possible, and I need to explain so that it would be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead but briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The files are kept at the Secretariat for National Defence, and the unit files are kept in a particular unit. Once mobilisation happens, a unit is called up, 1563-1/2, a unit is called up by code, and then call-up papers from the secretariat are sent to one and all. Out of all of these call-up papers, it is impossible to single out just certain names and surnames. Why? For example, Brdar, that is a last name that exists in all three communities. Then there were a lot of mixed marriages in Prijedor. So from one street two brothers, one married a Croat woman and the other one married a Muslim woman, so how could one of them just get call-up papers? And then if one person would go to the mobilisation site and say, Well, where is my -- where are my call-up papers? And the courier service functioned. So if necessary, I can provide further explanations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It will do for the time being. Could you now take a look at paragraph 10. It has to do with Mladen Stojanovic Detachment, and you say that after mobilisation and manning performed on the order of the regional TO Staff, it was went to the Urije airport and placed at the premises of the aircraft hangar. Its main task was to intervene in case of an interethnic conflict in the territory of Prijedor. Were there any Muslims in this detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And holding responsible posts, at that. Should I mention some names?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead. Tell us who held command positions?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Canic, Nedzad, assistant commander for logistics; a very important position. I spoke about that yesterday when I spoke about Major Aziz Selimbegovic. So it is the same function but the rank is lower. Enver Dracic, Ernest Badnjevic, Ivica Sikic [phoen] was commander of the 2nd Company, a Croat. So as I said yesterday, we made an effort and this was usually in TO units that I commanded. We strictly took this into account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the obvious questions here are whether mobilisation here is the same as the mobilisation mentioned in paragraph 8. Is that the September 1991 mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then second question: The persons you mentioned, did they stay in the Mladen Stojanovic Detachment for the remainder of 1991, 1992? Could you tell us whether they stayed in their positions; and if so -- if not, until when they had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While they were in the hangar at Mrakovica, they were in these units. Later in the month of May, the Army of Republika Srpska was established and all these TO units, and the detachment too went to the battalion of the 43rd Brigade. Most stayed on. Some went out for work obligation. There were professors, teachers, engineers. I can give you the specific names of certain persons who had to work according to work obligation, and there were those who volunteered, who said that they asked for that. And let us be frank, there are some who didn't want to be transferred to this battalion, but there are many who did want to. There were many officers and individuals. I can give you an example or two?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many non-Serbs stayed also when it was -- had become the battalion of the 43rd Brigade? How many non-Serbs did remain in leading positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot answer that question exactly because I went to fight for the corridor and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, fine. It is no problem. If you can't answer the question, we can't push to you do that. If you can't, you can't. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. What is your knowledge? How long did the command personnel stay at the TO?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said up until the establishment of the battalion. Let me just say this: Professor Susic stayed in the detachment until the very end. Badnjevic, Ernest, stayed until the very end when he was transferred to the 5th Brigade. Ernest is a businessman in Prijedor today and I can give many such examples, but I need a bit of time to focus; however, there were quite a few who did stay on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We mentioned command personnel. What about ethnic representation? Was ethnic representation present in the case of ordinary soldiers too?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that. When I went to Omarska with Vahid Ceric to report there, that's when these TO units had been mobilised. I already said there were 600-something Serbs, 500-something Muslims, and 87 Croats, so we did take that into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was September 1991. What about April? These same persons, members of the TO, were they there in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as territorial units are concerned, we didn't change anything there. And some people from the detachment had already transferred to the battalions. I already said that battalions were being prepared in the 43rd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask for one clarification. Mr. Javoric, you -- a minute ago you referred to people staying in the detachment until the very end. What do you mean by "the very end"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up until the establishment of the units of the battalion; that is to say, until the battalions were established. That is to say, all these units, the sabotage detachment that I commanded, then the Mladen Stojanovic Detachment. According to their place of residence and according to personnel needs, they came to man these battalions, so these TO units were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please help me, when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, battalions were established at different points in time. Some in June, some in May. I cannot say exactly now. I already told you that I went for the corridor breakthrough so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted to know the time. And now you said some in June, some in May. Which year?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No speaking at audible volume. No speaking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These territorial units, and you said that their composition was mixed. Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes they were. May I explain? When mobilisation took place of the territorial units, I already said that they had to do with a particular territory. They are mobilised in the same way as the manoeuvre units of the TO and the JNA; that is to say, they come to the mobilisation sites, they report there, and then they are given their weapons, that is to say, those that match their VES, and also because that was the conclusion of the council. On this occasion they were given ammunition as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is a VS; could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] VES is military occupational specialty; that is to say, every soldier is either an infantryman or a signalsman or an artilleryman or so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'm going ask you something that you may or may not know. Do you know who Ibro Alibegovic is? Was he in some unit in Prijedor. He's a colonel.

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now paragraph 11, please. Let us take a look at this. You say: "Other units were mobilised based on our assessment." Could you just tell us briefly what you meant by "other units"?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Prijedor that year, there was mobilisation on several occasions. Some of these mobilisations were based on the decisions of the Council for National Defence; others on orders from the republic staff. These other units -- I mean, how do I explain this? First of all, the territorial structure units were mobilised, and they were the most important for the municipality. In this way, the unit that guarded the biscuit factory that worked for Kras Zagreb - that's a very important facility - and that is the unit that was the first to be mobilised. Then the unit for Tukovi was mobilised where the wells are that provide water for the town of Prijedor. Then there was another unit that was mobilised --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I interrupt you. First, could you speak more slowly because otherwise your words will be lost. And second --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Second, would you not spontaneously give all kind of explanations once you've answered the question. The question -- one of the previous questions, for example, was were they armed. Your answer was yes. Now, that is for the time being enough. If Mr. Lukic wants further explanations, he'll ask for it. So would you refrain from expounding on brief answers you've given to clear questions. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something about paragraph 19 of your statement now. You said that despite the warning, when you were returning through Kozarac, you did go to Kozarac. Why did you go despite the warning?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two reasons. One: Because I had excellent co-operation with all the territorial units, and I thought that this warning did not involve any danger for me. They said that on the road there were Green Berets that were armed. Secondly, I wanted to see something for the very first time in my life. There was talk to the effect that the Green Berets were being armed, that the Serbs were being armed, and I had never seen any such thing in all my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where was it that you were actually coming back from?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Benkovac, which is part of Mrakovica, part of Kozara. That's where the Dr. Mladen Stojanovic Detachment had been transferred. I was going back to Prijedor and that was the shortest route to take, and I heard through communications equipment that the road had been blocked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both the question and the answer are already in paragraph 19. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the composition of the Dr. Mladen Stojanovic Detachment that was deployed in Mrakovica at that moment?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as it was at the airport or, rather, in the airport settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mixed?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in Kozarac, was there a Territorial Defence unit deployed there?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was mobilised at the same time as the other unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did it have its command?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the territorial unit in Kozarac, a Muslim or a Serb?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now let's go to paragraph 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need the following page in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the whole of what you -- what the witness told us about coming back and wanting to see with his own eyes the Green Berets, when exactly was that? Time-frame.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in the first half of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1992, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 22, you mention Niko Drincic. You say that he was with you in the barracks in the operative room when you heard that the soldiers in Hambarine had been attacked. You describe here the incident. Can you tell us what ethnicity was Niko Drincic?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Croat, captain first class.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long did he stay in the VRS or rather the JNA or rather the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a long time. He had a degree. He was an engineer. The mine was still opened. That's why he was sent there to be engaged in work -- employment, and then he became the general manager of a department there. I don't know exactly when he left, but we were together in the barracks when the attack on Hambarine had started.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You went to the corridor; right? Do you know whether in the units of the VRS there were Croats and Muslims who were also engaged on breaking through the corridor?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, always, please, a time-frame exactly so that we have the chronology clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When? When did that happen? What month?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corridor was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you -- you're again asked to slow down because we'll lose part of your testimony if you continue to speak at this speech -- at this speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The only thing that was recorded was -- or, rather, nothing was recorded -- recorded. When did the operation corridor start, in what month?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation corridor started in May. It had started even before that, but the Slijepcevic Battalion from Prijedor was first engaged on the 28th of May. I apologise. It was in June. I misspoke. It was not in May. It was on the 28th of June when they entered Modrica. The passage was liberated. And after that, the corridor was passable. I apologise about the error of one month.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the relationship between the fighters of different nationalities in Prijedor and on -- in the theatre of war?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good, harmonious. They were all colleagues there. They were brothers. Shall I expand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Lukic, you could ask the witness: When you said that Croats and Muslims were also engaged in breaking through the corridor, and that you said was in June, what was approximately the number? Was it 20 per cent non-Serbs, 40 per cent non-Serbs, 1 per cent non-Serbs? What was approximately the -- the quantitative involvement of Croats and Muslims in that operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't give you a precise answer. It was a long time ago, but I know that in the 2nd Battalion there were Croats. I know who their company commander was. I was more attached to them when we started the Operation Corridor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know whether there were any non-Serbs, Muslims and Croats, in other battalions than the one you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there were. Ernest Badnjevic was a member of the 2nd Battalion of the 5th Brigade and remained a member until the end of the war. There were others as well, but at the moment, I can't -- or, rather, yes, I've just remembered. Somebody's whose nickname was Schmidt. He was also a professor or an electrical engineer. He stayed until the very end. And after that, he found employment at a school as a teacher. His name was Emir Susic and his nickname was Schmidt. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm interested in numbers rather than in specific persons. In the 2nd Battalion you said there were Croats. Were there any Muslims in the 2nd Battalion to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not received the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Nobody received translation at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'll repeat my questions -- question. Were there any Muslims in the 2nd Battalion where you told us that was -- there were Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were Muslims in the 2nd Battalion as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember exactly, but I believe that two, if not even five, were killed during the operations. I can't give you the exact data. As I've told you, I was more attached to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not asking how many were killed. I asked you how many there were. You can't tell us --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really can't give you a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You can't tell us also percentage-wise on whether it was a very, very small minority or whether it was a substantial number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The battalions were set up in a territorial sense. In Ljubija, there were more Muslims than Croats. And the company -- therefore, in percentage terms, they were not represented to that extent, but there were some, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Among the fighters of different ethnicities, were there any differences in the food they were given, where they slept, the salaries they received?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was the same across the board. There were no differences in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the families received humanitarian aid in Prijedor and its environs. Were there any differences there according to ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none whatsoever. The fighters were together on the front line, and the families were together in the rear. It was all the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at a document and the number is 1D5333.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar informs that under that number there is no document, Mr. Lukic. Could you please verify the accuracy of the number you gave. It's recorded as 1D5333.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the number I have. Give me one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you sure that you have released the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are trying to check if it's in the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, meanwhile, you move ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have -- can we find it on the basis of the doc ID which is known to the Chamber as being 1D19-1173. That document apparently is known. Let's have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's the document I need.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before us we have a list that I already showed you. And at the end, we can see that the list was signed by Miso Rodic. Do you know what was Miso Rodic's position at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Miso Rodic was the -- or, rather, he is now the chief of department in Prijedor for protection of veterans and fighters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in the English translation I see Miso Radic. Could we look at the relevant page in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It is. "Rodic" should be corrected, obviously. Mr. Rodic should testify in this case as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we see the respective page in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't know how many pages --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page. It's on the last page, his signature and name. It's handwritten so that's why maybe there was confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you co-operate with Mr. Rodic's office in your everyday work?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as well as with all the others because of the nature of my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, tell us how you co-operate.

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a director of the welfare centre, we co-operate with Miso to help the families of those who had been killed during the war irrespective of their ethnicity. Of the hard-up families, we give them food, medicines, clothes. We try to help them to exercise their rights. I have three lawyers at the centre, and they represent them pro bono when needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, another question. This list bears a date, 15th December, 2014. Was that prepared for this trial? Was that -- what -- what is the relevance if we don't know the date when the original documents were prepared?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document is prepared on the 15th of December, 2014. It's prepared by Mr. Rodic for this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And what is the basis for it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We asked him to give us the list of people on his -- in his register of non-Serb ethnicity who were fighters and members of VRS during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What does it mean "during the war"? There are several years, but we don't have -- I don't see any reference. Perhaps in the last line, date of status, 3rd of November, 1999, that should be explained. I have no idea what the resource of all of that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Couldn't he provide the register itself rather than make an excerpt from the register?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can do that but we tried to shorten our evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, yes. But could I then ask you, if it says: Date of status, as we see on our screen now, the 3rd of November, 1999, and these apparently are conscripts, now could you tell us whether that means that mister, and the name is there, with a certain number who was born in 1973 was on the 3rd of November 1999 a conscript? Is that how we have to understand it? Because I have difficulties in understanding exactly what the "date of status" means, because we have many there, sometimes 2000, 2004, 1997. Could you explain to us what that means, the date of status?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can see here that when it says "status" it says, for example, "military obligation ceased due do old age in 2004," but we will have probably the best --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but where this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- from Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that part also -- there apparently is an index attached to it, and we have not looked at that index. Does the index give the explanation or -- I mean, unless the witness would know anything about it. Do you know anything about this document, Witness? Do you know anything about the content of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can give you my comment. The list that we see -- could it please be zoomed in -- no, don't bother, it's okay. These are members of non-Serb ethnicity who were members of various battalions and who stayed their members until the end of the war or were killed or had other obligations and left the unit before that. There's a name and the year of birth and for how long he was kept on the files of that unit or the national defence. On the right-hand side, it says "ceased" and why he left, age, died, so on and so forth. Those records still exist, and those who are of non-Serb ethnicity are still in Prijedor. They live there. I recognise a lot of those people on the list who were members of our units. I'm very grateful to have the list before me to jog my memory of those days. For each and every one of them, I can tell you where they were, what they did, and so on and so forth. And especially Miso Rodic can do that because he was working on that. He was also an intelligence organ. That was his speciality. He had worked at the Secretariat for National Defence for a long time, and then he was assigned to a new duty as the chief of Department for Veterans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apparently you recognise some names. Mr. Lukic, first of all, you say list of conscripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Conscripts of what? Is that conscript of the VRS, is it conscripts of -- what is it, is it TO? What are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me? Are you putting this question to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This list I see before me, when it says "military conscript" it means military conscript who was deployed to a particular unit, battalions, et cetera. Perhaps he was in a territorial unit, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it is the battalions that were there up until the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But is this VRS? Is this TO list? What are we looking at at this moment; if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This list -- I mean, I only have the first page here. But here on the first page I see Croats, mostly Croats, who stayed in units --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not asking you -- simply the first page of this document reads: List of conscripts. Added to this is Croats. There is the number 381. List of conscripts of what exactly? That's the only question I'm putting to you. Is this conscripts of the VRS? Is this conscripts of the TO? What is it? If you know. If you don't know, tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I see here before me were people who were in battalions; that is to say, of the Army of Republika Srpska. There were units of the TO, and the Army of Republika Srpska was established, and what I see here is the persons who remained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see that if you have a list of names, that these are persons named. This doesn't come as a surprise to me. You said VRS TO. Which of the two? Is this a TO list or is this a VRS list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This list that I see before me was taken from the files of the Secretariat of National Defence. How individuals were deployed to battalions; that is to say, once the VRS had already been established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does this mean that 381 Croats were conscripts in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And served as such?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is this only about persons in Prijedor or is it persons from elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I see here, I mean, I can give you a few names, quite a few, from Prijedor. I cannot remember all of them now, but I know so many people in person; name, surname, occupation and so on. People who were with us up until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You've told us that several times. I'm trying to find out what this list is, not whether you recognise certain persons on it. Would it mean that if, for example, someone is here reported --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as having been born in 1937 - and we find such numbers, for example, on the first page in the original - that therefore at the beginning of the war, being at an age of 40, 45 years that they were conscripts in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Many, when they report to join a unit, the command would not refuse, although some of them were already beyond the required age. For example, we have this man from Ljubija, a Muslim, Hodzic, I've forgotten his first name. He was very old but he came and joined us, although he was very old, and stayed on with us. And it says here when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, again, you emphasise that you recognise certain names, but you're apparently not able to answer my question, whether these were conscripts at the time, what exactly this list is, to what date it refers, whether they were on active duty, yes or no. Do you know whether these persons listed here were on active duty during the war, all of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The very form of this document, perhaps it should have been worked out in a different way. But I can tell you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me -- if you say that the list should have worked out in a different way, that's not the kind of answers I'm seeking at this moment. Mr. Lukic, please put focused questions to the witness on this list and make the questions such that the Chamber understands what it exactly is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell us now: As for this first page, who are the persons that you know were with you in the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anusic, Zoran, mother Viktorija. He was in Slavonia from day one and stayed on until the very end. He was a driver and mechanic. He is also a sportsman playing handball.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we're not asking what sports they did. You were referring to who exactly? Which one? Is that the fifth on the list, Anusic Zoran, mother Viktorija.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, Witness, Witness, stay a bit away from the screen and come a bit closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we have to enlarge this, Your Honour. Oh, it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can ask the Registrar to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I had already asked for this to be zoomed in a bit, but it's all right. Well, yes, I did ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't need English, probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said there was no need to do that immediately after that. Let's -- he said this person was with you in Slovenia. When?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Slavonia. When?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not in Slavonia, but Zoran was there in the battalion. I know that full well. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In September. He left with the 43rd Brigade in 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was in 1991. So it cannot be VRS because the VRS did not exist in 1991, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know why you're pressing the witness. He said he stayed with us until the end of the war. He stated clearly. We have it in the transcript -- [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm trying --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know you don't like this document, but that's how it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no problems with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Obviously you do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, first of all, calm down. Is that clear to you? I can only --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is truth --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- and we will introduce it. You should try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, don't interrupt me again. Wait for a second. I'm trying desperately to find out what this document is, that's one. And second, I'm desperately trying to find out what the witness can tell us about the document. Because whether I like a document or not is not relevant. What is important for this Chamber that it is able to understand the evidence that it -- that is presented before it. That's what I'm doing. Nothing more. Nothing less. And I invited you to put focused questions, including such that we know what this document is about. The witness told us that this could be VRS and TO, and the witness now tells us that he remembers that one of the persons on this list was in Slavonia in 1991, and then I had difficulties to reconcile that with what the witness told us, that this could be VRS because according to my knowledge, but please correct me if I'm wrong, the VRS was not yet established in September 1991. I leave it to that at this moment. I think it's also --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. No, you may not. Mr. Mladic is also supposed not to speak aloud. Mr. Lukic, you may now be aware, the Chamber has in understanding the source of this document, what it exactly tells us. You can understand that from the questions that were put to the witness both by me and by my colleagues. I invite you to put focused questions to the witness to the extent he has knowledge of the matters contained in this list so that the Chamber is able to understand what it is. And whether we like it or not is another matter, it's got nothing do with it. We have to analyse what it is. We'll take the break first and we expect you to put such questions to the witness after the break. Witness, you may follow the usher. We'll take a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to enter the courtroom. Meanwhile, I can use the time briefly and I'll briefly deal with a document which was tendered through Witness Milorad Sajic. On 2nd of December, during the testimony of Milorad Sajic, the Prosecution tendered a military diary which the Chamber marked for identification as P6970 and it was placed under seal. The Prosecution indicated that it would upload into e-court a reduced version of the diary. On the 16th of January of this year, the Prosecution informed the Chamber via an e-mail that it had uploaded an excerpt of the diary under Rule 65 ter number 8656b, and the Registry is hereby instructed to replace P6970 with the newly uploaded version and admits the document into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm very sorry to interrupt, but if I might just request that the Registry hold off. It -- the document -- the full version was on my exhibit list for this witness and I'll have to change some page numbers and it might create some technical difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Madam Registrar is invited not to enforce the decision yet but to postpone that until further order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you're ready, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Javoric, just briefly, please, tell us about the first page of this document. Who is it that you know from this page? And tell us whether you know whether this person was a member of the VRS and whether you know up until when this person remained in the VRS? Just from the first page.

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Atlija Miroslav was in VRS --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not understand the rest of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat what he said after giving a name and told that the person was in the VRS. What did you then add, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot exactly up until when. I was not a personnel officer in the battalion who kept these files. Rather, I was a senior officer and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I stop you there. If you don't know something, you don't know. That's good enough for us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lawyer, may I? You asked me whether I knew someone who's from the army and I said yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, when I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- intervened, it's not for you to say who should proceed, yes or no, and at what point in time. You told us that -- let me read it again. That Atlija Miroslav was in the VRS and you don't know until when. Any other person on this first page you recognise?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you a bit about Miroslav Atlija. Where does he live today?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Prijedor he's involved in sports, kickboxing. Bakau [phoen], Zlatko.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a watchmaker at the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When, nowadays or before the war?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He works there to this day. I do apologise. You asked me who I recognise. I mean, I cannot know who stayed until the very end. I was a senior officer, a ranking officer. I mean, come on. Don't ask me to answer things that I cannot. I mean, I'm saying this for the benefit of the people who are listening. I mean, it would not be nice for me to say that somebody was not there, and then if he did stay on until the end, I wouldn't be saying the truth and these people wouldn't want to hear something like that. Well, yes, I like you too. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please, people from this page. Just tell us who you know from this list and where they live nowadays, if you know.

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said Brener, Zoran. He died. He was in the army. He had a masters degree. And then his two sons, Zoran. So Becner Bojan lives in Prijedor nowadays. He is the director of the centre for pensioners. I have a good co-operation with him. He has a degree in economics. I have a good co-operation with him. Do you need anything else? Mr. Lawyer, I tell you about all these things that I know and then you insist on the date. It's not fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please don't be angry with me. We see that you don't know dates, so we're not asking you about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, tell me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you don't know the answer to a question, simply say, "I don't know." That's good enough. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: However, the record does not reflect what you said about Zoran Anusic. Do you know whether he was a member of the VRS and where he lives today?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoran Anusic was a member of the VRS. And I added something, perhaps I wasn't supposed to, that he lives in -- that he lives in Prijedor, is a mechanic, has two children, and that he is a driver. Is that enough?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you say he died?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He's a driver.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But at --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who died?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, can we begin again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do not bury --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you just hold on please. I'm talking. Page 29, line 1: "I've already said ... Zoran, he died. He was in the army. He had a masters degree. And then his two sons, Zoran. So Becner Bojan ..." Were you not talking about the same Anusic, Zoran, here? I'm asking you a question, sir. Which Zoran were you talking about on the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not the same one. These are two completely different people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which one were you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Anusic Zoran is a youngish man. He was in the VRS --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I stop you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and I said that he is an auto mechanic and so on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I assist, ten lines down --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which Zoran died? Which Zoran is the one who died? Can you just tell us? That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Becner, Zoran. He died. He had a masters degree, two sons. All of this has to be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see anyone else that you know on this page, a person who was in the VRS and where do they live today?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me the second page. I'm done with the first one. If I were to ask you questions given that kind of time distance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, would you please refrain from commenting on this kind of matters. Mr. Lukic, you changed --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It's my instinct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then keep control over your instinct. Mr. Lukic, you started asking whether the witness recognised any person on this list. In the last phrase, the last time you asked: "It was do you see anyone else that you know on this page, a person who was in the VRS..." That's a different question from the one you started with; that is, whether the witness recognises any persons. But we're not going through the whole of this list to find out whether the witness recognises persons and knows what their education is, whether they live or whether they died or not without understanding what the list is. I would suggest, as a matter of fact, that if the witness who drafted the list appears as a witness, that we'll ask such further questions and that it be MFI'd for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Then I do not have any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, the document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D05333 receives MFI D896, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Javoric. That was all we had for you at the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Javoric, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You find Mr. Traldi to your right. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. And may I urge you again not to go beyond what is asked and to refrain from any critical comments on persons who ask you questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I have a couple of matters that I'd just like to clarify arising out of your direct examination. First, in paragraph 27 of your statement, you discuss a task you were given to look for people to join Slijepcevic Battalion tasked with opening the corridor, and that after final preparations in Gornja Lamovita, you departed on the 25th of May, 1992. In light of the correction you made this morning during direct examination, that paragraph should be the 25th of June that you departed for the corridor; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. I did not even notice this mistake, the mistake being the 25th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I have another question just to clarify. Another matter on direct. There were two Territorial Defence units, the Mladen Stojanovic Detachment and a reconnaissance and sabotage detachment, that you mentioned, and I wasn't clear from your testimony on direct whether your evidence was that they were manoeuvre units or territorial units. Can you tell us which it was?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both were territorial units. The Dr. Mladen Stojanovic Detachment in Prijedor and the reconnaissance detachment was collecting intelligence for the municipality and higher-ranking unit. The first unit was ranked as a battalion, and the latter unit was ranked as a platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, yesterday Mr. Lukic asked you if you recalled the name of the Muslim who was the president of Prijedor municipality in 1991 and you weren't able to remember. It was Professor Cehajic?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cehajic. Let me correct your pronunciation. Cehajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I appreciate that, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muhamed was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Muhamed Cehajic, who had been the president of Prijedor municipality in 1991, now that you've recalled that, you also recall, don't you, that he was murdered in Omarska camp in 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that. I was never in any of the collection centres or camps. I never toured any of them. I don't know what went on there. Therefore, I'm not aware of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So when you say in your statement, sir, that the VRS did not secure any of the camps or collection centres in Prijedor, you don't actually know who was involved in securing those camps, do you?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only tell you what I do know. The immediate security was provided by the TO of Slobodan Kuruzovic, whereas the wider ring was the VRS. I was not there. I discharged other duties. I can only tell you what I heard from other people. I can only convey those words.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, what you've just described, that refers to Trnopolje camp; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't consider that a camp. It was a collection centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's not focus on the word for the moment. It was Trnopolje where the immediate security was provided by men under Kuruzovic's command; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. The Serbian TO. Because in addition to the TO that I commanded, there was another one and they had nothing to do with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you. And I will get to questions about your TO and Mr. Kuruzovic's TO, but let's just take it step by step. Now, I want to talk about your career a little bit. You served in both the 5th Kozara Brigade and the 43rd Motorised Brigade of the VRS at different points during the war; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, by the end of the war, the men who commanded both those brigades in May 1992, Pero Colic and Vladimir Arsic, had been promoted to the rank of general; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, turning now to the Territorial Defence before the war. Now, you mention the regional TO Staff based in Banja Luka and you identify Milan Krneta as its commander in paragraph 7 of your statement. Now, beginning in September 1991, the command --

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Beginning in September 1991, the commander of the regional TO Staff was Colonel Petar Spasojevic; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But then he was removed and replaced by another. And both of them were infantrymen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, when were you suggesting that Colonel Spasojevic was removed?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in fact, he remained commander of the regional TO Staff up till the creation of the VRS, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. Just like I could not remember about Cehajic yesterday. I can't remember about him today.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's look at 65 ter 06546.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an order from the Banja Luka Regional Territorial Defence Staff dated the 12th of March, 1992, in this case to the Sanski Most TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could look at the end of the document in both languages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be zoomed in just a little, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For the moment, I'd ask that we zoom in on the signature and the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So as of the 12th of March, 1992, Colonel Spasojevic remained the commander of the regional TO, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could look back to the first page and zoom in on the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The third paragraph --

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You do, actually, sir. It begins with the words, "Ucilju." And that reads: "In order to create the optimal conditions for the life, work, and complete security of the employees at TO headquarters and the complete security of TO facilities, pursuant to strictly confidential order number 238-1 of the 5th Corps issued on 9 March 1992 ..." Now, I'm not going to ask you about the details of the order. What I'm going to ask you is, it's correct that as of 12th of March, the regional TO Staff was implementing orders from the command of the 5th Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's passing this order down to one of the municipal TO Staffs along the chain of command; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 06546.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 06546 receives Exhibit P7118, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning to the Prijedor Territorial Defence for a moment. You mentioned two Territorial Defences in Prijedor in your statement and just now: Your Territorial Defence, the official one; and one set up by the SDS commanded by Slobodan Kuruzovic. Now Kuruzovic, aside from being a SDS member, also fought in Western Slavonia as a battalion command in the 343rd Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And now back to the regional TO Staff for a moment. Now, Colonel Spasojevic who we just saw was the commander of the regional TO Staff. He was your immediate superior officer during this period; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And his office was in the 5th Corps headquarters in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you say in your statement that was on Marsala Tito Street. That's what it was called before the war began, right, the street?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have mixed things together. My staff was in Marsala Tito Street in Prijedor. Those are two different things. The command of my staff was one thing and the command of the regional staff was another thing. I'm afraid you did not pay attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll try and focus very carefully, sir. I want to look, then, at one of the things your staff did, the mobilisation in September 1991. You were asked yesterday at transcript pages 31384 and 31385 who orders mobilisation, and you testified that: "We receive an order from the District Staff and the District Staff receives an order from the republic staff." Now, in fact, what happened with the September 1991 mobilisation is that you received an order from the District TO Staff but they received their order from the 5th Corps of the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who they received their order from. But this was common practice for the Republican Staff to issue orders to the regional staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and then the regional staff issued their order to us and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the end of the answer got lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32021, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an article from Oslobodjenje on the 1st of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just for ease of locating, it's the second article down in the ride column in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what we read is: "Yesterday, the BH government assessed as an unconstitutional and illegal act the general mobilisation in the area of the Banja Luka Corps of the JNA proclaimed by its commander, General Nikola Uzelac." Now that's the truth, isn't it, that the mobilisation in September 1991 was ordered by the commander of the 5th Corps, General Uzelac?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not read Oslobodjenje. I told you who our orders came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is it -- are -- are you telling this Trial Chamber that the average newspaper reader in Bosnia was aware of who had ordered the mobilisation you were conducting but you yourself were not?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you yesterday that the general who was the chief of the Republican Staff came to Prijedor, we went to Mr. Cehajic's office and talked about mobilisation, and I suppose that the republican staff sent his -- its order to the regional staff and then they sent it to us. Cehajic -- Fikret was with me when we went to Cehajic's office and ordered the mobilisation. I don't see anything wrong with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you were asked to answer a question, not to speculate on whether someone considers something to be wrong or right. Just answer the questions. Tell us about any facts you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 32021 receives exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not received any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 32021 receives Exhibit P7119, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You mentioned other mobilisations on direct examination. There was also a mobilisation in November 1991 in Prijedor; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that was after the 343rd and 5th Brigades had been in Western Slavonia for about a month and then returned; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them returned. Only some elements were sent on furlough by the command. Some were in the theatre of war; the others were on furlough. That's how things were done at the time. I was in Prijedor, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, during this November 1991 mobilisation, the rule was that people could, if they were willing to go to the front, be mobilised. They could also, if they were not willing to go to the front, return their weapons to the headquarters; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if they were mobilised by the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the people that returned their weapons were mostly Muslims and Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who were mobilised by the staff and who came to us saying they did not want to go back surrendered their weapons. Most of them did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was whether those who did so were mostly Muslims and Croats. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were also Serbs who, for some reason, did not want to stay either because they were wounded or they were under their family's pressure. There were Serbs as well, or people from mixed marriages who wanted to move out, and they did eventually. I don't know if you understand me. Please can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- can -- can I get the interpretation of the Judge's words, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will not receive the interpretation of my words if you continue to speak yourself and instead of following my clear hand signs that I want you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are now doing the same. The question was not whether there were also Serbs. The question was whether they were mostly Muslims and Croats. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A simple yes would have done half a page ago. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'd ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Lukic, we -- at the beginning of this session, we had some discussion about the list you presented and which I think you said was provided by Mr. Rodic, if I remember well. Now, you -- I take it that you want to tender later that document, prepare that list. Now that list is apparently extract from other sources. Have you or will you disclose to the Prosecution the sources of this list used by Mr. Rodic to make this list in 2014?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are ready to copy the whole document. We have no problem with that. Only I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the whole document? Do you mean the document which was MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or even more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If there is anything else, we are willing to provide, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the basis for it because this apparently is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I learned from this witness is that Mr. Rodic also keeps track of different nationalities and that he has this kind of list in his archives as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the only thing --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I haven't checked with Mr. Rodic yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only thing is in order to avoid that when Mr. Rodic appears as a witness that we have further debates about how to verify the accuracy of what he prepared in 2014, that there's access to both parties - and, of course, it's your witness, so I take it that you'll take the first steps - so as to be available to verify the accuracy of the list drafted when we hear what the list exactly is about. Please keep that in mind. We take a break and we resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could you give us an indication as to how much more time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I expect to finish in this session, Mr. President, but not -- not in the next few minutes, anyway. But half of this session or a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Half of the session or a little bit more. Then you would stay more or less within your time assessment. Taking the whole session, you would not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And a few minutes -- I think your estimate was one hour. One and a half. Then you have 45 minutes left. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's right. I'd initially thought, Mr. President, I might need a few minutes extra on the basis of direct, but it appears I might not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to turn now to May 1992 in Prijedor. You say in paragraph 31 of your statement you were never a member of the SDS or the Crisis Staff or the War Presidency. You were, however, a member of the National Defence Council; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of the council.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the president of the council was Dr. Stakic; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What you have just said, that was precisely so. I was not a member --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the National Defence Council by virtue of my position but not of anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Kuruzovic, Mr. Arsic, Mr. Zeljaja, all also members of the National Defence Council; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The National Defence Council, or, rather, the State Defence Council, not National Defence Council, and the chief of SUP --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is speaking too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness. Witness, you're speaking too fast, and if you would simply answer the question that was put to you, whether Mr. Kuruzovic, Mr. Arsic, and Mr. Zeljaja were also member of, as you clarified now, the State Defence Council. Were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, can we have P2871.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, these are the minutes of the 4th meeting of the council held on the 15th of May, 1992, starting at 10.00 in the morning. And on the list of attendees, we see your name in the third row. And we see at point 1 decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff. Looking at the bottom of the page in English, we see that Dr. Milomir Stakic and Slavko Budimir participated in the discussion and that the draft decision was approved under the proviso that a representative of the garrison in Prijedor be added to the proposed list of members of the Crisis Staff. Now, I have two focused questions about the Crisis Staff. First, this was being established pursuant to a decision by the political leadership of the Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's start with yes or no. The Prijedor Crisis Staff was being established here pursuant to a decision by the political leadership of the Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what was said, but I was not a politician.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who said it?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who was it who presented the agenda, and I know that everybody was in charge of presenting one item of the agenda. I believe that it was Dr. Stakic who dealt with this particular item.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it was he who said it was being established pursuant to a decision by the political leadership; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And, yes, now that you've jogged my memory, I can answer. Yes. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence that there had earlier in 1992 been a Serb Crisis Staff in Prijedor as well. Were you also aware of that Serb Crisis Staff? And I'm asking, just to be very precise, I'm simply asking if you were aware of that Crisis Staff's existence.

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning to page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a reference to items 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, I'm sorry, we'll need page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a set of conclusions. And at point 3 we see the conclusion: "Start the transformation of both TO Staffs and form a unified command for control and command of all the units formed in the territory of the municipality." Now, the reference to both TO Staffs means both your staff and Mr. Kuruzovic's TO Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the effect of this decision was to take those two TO Staffs that were already under the control of what was then still the 343rd Motorised Brigade and to begin formally integrating them into the brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only talk about my staff and say that it was under that command. I don't know much about Mr. Kuruzovic's SDS staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, could we have 65 ter 31952, page 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this will be a part of Mr. Kuruzovic's testimony in the Stakic case. Now, he was asked --

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, carefully listen to what will be read to you, because there's only one authentic copy of this document; that is, the English one. So carefully listen to what Mr. Traldi reads to you as evidence given by Mr. Kuruzovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now beginning, for the Chamber and the Defence's reference, at the end of line 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Kuruzovic says: "About the second conclusion, the headquarters of the Territorial Defence should be included in the single command. As far as I remember, it was later called the Command of the Region to avoid having several military organisations. Therefore, the staff of the Territorial Defence commanded by Rade Javoric, and the staff in which I was, which was not really a military organisation, were formally united and resubordinated to the command of the region. That is, Commander Arsic." And he explains and identifies the military post number. And then beginning at line 16, he says: "And I also said that on the 16th or the 17th, I received an order to the effect that I and what was referred to as my staff and the staff of Mr. Javoric without any exceptions should be attached to the command of the region, that is, of the brigade, military postbox 4777." Now, first, that military post number, 4777, was the military post number for what was the 343rd Motorised Brigade of the JNA and later the 43rd Motorised Brigade of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 343rd Motorised Brigade, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what Mr. Kuruzovic testified to here is the truth, isn't it, both of your Territorial Defence organisations were formally united and resubordinated to the command of the region to Commander Arsic after this meeting on the 15th of May?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about 1992, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We are.

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that in December we received that order and in January we were already under the JNA command, and I hear only now that Kuruzovic was supposed to do the same. In January, we were already in the barracks under the JNA command. You will find that in my statement. You will see who was to be handed over, how. Everybody but Vahid Ceric did that. Everybody signed that. We were already under the command of --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you about what happened in December or January. I'm asking you what Mr. Kuruzovic is saying about his TO being formally subordinated as of this time to the command of the region. That's the truth, isn't it, after the 15th of May --

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't comment on Kuruzovic's words.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's have P2871 back; page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, at point 3, where it refers to both TO Staffs and forming them into a unified command, you agreed with me earlier "both TO Staffs" refers to your staff and Mr. Kuruzovic's; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we had been resubordinated a long time before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And a unified command of the region called the Prijedor Region Command and later the Prijedor operational and Tactical Group was, in fact, formed after this meeting, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADE JAVORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that it was its name, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
